messages:
nina: Heads-up: launching the "Deprecation Clarity" initiative next week. Goal: make every public SDK change self-explanatory in docs + release notes, with clear timers and migration guidance. Full playbook: https://redwood.internal/docs/deprecation-playbook :sparkles:
omar: Nice. What's different from past deprecation notes?
nina: Three concrete changes: 1) standardized severity levels (low/medium/high) with fixed minimum runways: low=30d, medium=60d, high=120d; 2) deprecation metadata required in PRs and package manifests; 3) auto-generated migration snippets and a public "sunset" date shown in docs and Console banners.
lia: Are the runways flexible for enterprise requests? Some customers need bespoke schedules.
nina: Yes. Enterprise exceptions possible via support ticket (tag: depr-exemption). PM + Eng must approve within 5 business days; we can set a per-tenant pinned compatibility flag if granted.
release-bot: Canary job: deprecation-playbook-canary scheduled for 2025-10-01T18:00Z. Will exercise metadata parsing, banner generation, and snippet attachments.
ryan: Example of the PR metadata format?
docs-bot: Example (add to PR body):```
deprecation-metadata: |
  severity: medium
  affected: sdk-js, sdk-py
  sunset: 2026-01-15
  migration_snippet: ./migrations/rename-foo-to-bar.js
  public_impact: true
```
omar: How does CI treat this? Will missing metadata block merges?
nina: CI will warn by default. Starting week 2 post-canary, PRs that touch public APIs without metadata will be blocked. Severity >= medium also requires PM sign-off and a runnable migration example (JS or Python).
lia: Migration snippets: autogenerated or hand-authored?
nina: Hybrid. Were shipping redwood-codemods for common patterns (param renames, default flips). Codemods will open a suggested migration snippet as a PR comment. Authors should verify and attach the snippet to the PR. Hand-authored snippets are fine and recommended for complex changes.
ryan: Docs UX: where will sunset dates show?
docs-bot: Sunset date will appear in reference pages as a header banner: "Deprecated (sunsets on 2026-01-15)" plus a severity badge. Console will show an in-product banner for active API keys 30 days before sunset for medium/high. Low shows only in release notes.
lia: Testing: can we run the migration snippet in CI? I worry about flaky examples.
nina: Examples-runner will execute snippets in an isolated harness; snippets may use replay fixtures. Failing snippet tests will add a label "migration-snippet-failed" and block severity >= medium until fixed.
omar: Backports? Are we backporting deprecation metadata to older minor branches?
nina: No automatic backports. We will only backport critical security or enterprise-agreed exemptions. For maintainers who want consistent history, we provide a migration job that can annotate past releases with best-effort metadata.
ryan: How do we communicate externally? Docs + console + changelog + email?
nina: All of the above. Standard comms: release notes + "migration guide" in docs, in-console banner for customers with active keys, and an email digest to subscribers with medium/high deprecations. Enterprise CSMs get a CSV export listing affected tenants.
docs-bot: Also adding a README badge for packages with attached migration snippets: [deprecation-ready]. Maintainers can opt-out if needed.
lia: Any billing or SLA impact when removing features?
nina: Deprecations don't change billing. If a change affects SLA, Eng + Product must note it in the PR and coordinate a rollout with the ops team.
omar: One more: how does this interact with compat-mode / runtime shims?
nina: Shims/compat flags are encouraged for high-impact changes. If a shim is provided, include its usage in the migration snippet and mark it in metadata (e.g., "compatibility_flag: REDWOOD_LEGACY_FOO"). Shims buy extra runway but we still publish a sunset date.
ryan: I'll add the docs templates and a checklist to the release playbook. ETA: PR by Friday.
nina: Thanks all. I'll post the short FAQ and the codemod repo link after the canary is green. :memo:
